newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros, EU fishing negotiations stalled.
newsitem.headline: Comoros, EU fishing negotiations stalled.

text.p: Negotiations between the Comoros and the European Union over renewing a fishing contract round the Indian Ocean islands ended in deadlock at the weekend, officials said on Sunday.
A three-year agreement for European deep-freeze tuna boats to fish off the Comoros expired on July 19, and no date has been set for the resumption of negotiations.
"The Comoros government asked us to grant it a certain time for reflection," Aronne Spezzani, of the EU Directorate General for Fishing, who led the five-member EU delegation, told Reuters.
Spezzani said the EU wanted to increase the number of deep-freeze tuna boats from 37 to 55 while maintaining the 4,500 tonnes annual limit.
The Comoros rejected this and proposed increasing the catch to 6,000 tonnes while maintaining the same number of boats, in return for an increase in EU aid.
"Since 37 boats have not been able to catch the allowed 4,500 tonnes, it is not possible to use the same number of boats to catch more than 4,500 tonnes," Spezzani said.
Comoran sources said that they suspected the total of fish caught was in fact higher than the quantity European fishermen officially declared.
